findings.evidence: Line 263-264: `hR.merge_smul_one_sub_smul (hS _ ht1 p hp) (1 + t)⁻¹ …` is the only occurrence of `hS` and of `hp` in the body; the remaining steps (lines 265-266) never mention `S`.
findings.fix: Drop `hS` and replace `hp : p ∈ S` by `hp : (1 + t) • p ∈ S`: `(hR : R.IsCollinearExactOn S) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) {p : V} (hp : (1 + t) • p ∈ S) : R.merge p (t • p) = (1 + t) • p`. `isCollinearExactOn_iff` (line 287) keeps `hS` and discharges the forward direction with `hR.merge_smul_eq_one_add_smul ht (hS _ (by linarith) p hp)`.
findings.issue: `IsCollinearExactOn.merge_smul_eq_one_add_smul` assumes closure of `S` under all positive rescalings (`hS`) plus `p ∈ S`, but the proof uses both only to produce the single membership `(1 + t) • p ∈ S`.

findings.evidence: Both uses in the body are at `s`: line 461 `hJ s p 0 le_rfl` and line 463 `hJ s _ _ (div_nonneg …)`. The sibling infrared lemma at line 489 is deliberately local in its hypotheses (`∀ᶠ p in 𝓝 0`, `ContinuousAt … a`), per its own docstring at lines 485-486; the collinear lemma is not.
findings.fix: Bind `s` before `hJ` and fix it there: `(s : Multiset V) (hJ : ∀ (a : V) (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → J (a ::ₘ t • a ::ₘ s) = J (R.merge a (t • a) ::ₘ s))`. `IsCollinearExact.isCollinearSafe` (line 468) still applies it, passing `hJ s`.
findings.issue: `IsCollinearExactOn.apply_smul_cons_one_sub_smul_cons` takes `s : Multiset V` as an explicit argument and states the conclusion at that `s`, yet requires `hJ` for *every* multiset; the proof instantiates `hJ` only at that same `s`. An observable with the merging property at one final state but not others is excluded for no reason.

summary: Two theorems carry hypotheses strictly stronger than their proofs use: a global rescaling-closure hypothesis on the set where only membership of the single rescaled point is needed, and an observable hypothesis quantified over all final states where only the one the theorem already fixes is needed. Otherwise the statements sit at the natural level and the special cases are derived from the general ones.
